name: Kerala Chicken Curry (Nadan Kozhi Curry)

fit.reason: 610 cal is within 400-650, 14g carbs is well under 35g, no seafood, chicken braise scales to 14. Published numbers clear the band (note: 610 sits at the top edge from 3 tbsp coconut oil over 3 servings, so recompute could approach the ceiling, but as published it passes).

duplicate.nearest_catalog: chicken-madras-curry (South Indian chicken + coconut milk + tomato + onion) and kuku-paka-swahili-coconut-chicken-curry (coconut+tomato chicken-thigh curry)
duplicate.evidence: Distinct dish: Madras is a curry-powder-based South Indian curry with carrots/bell pepper served over rice; Kuku Paka is East African Swahili. Kerala Nadan Kozhi is set apart by thin coconut milk + a curry-leaf / fennel-seed / pearl-onion tempering and a toasted whole-spice masala, and carries no starch in the plate. Also not a dupe of accepted burmese-chicken-dal-curry (dal-based) or thai-coconut-curry-pork-shoulder (Thai, pork). Three-of-four overlap with Madras (chicken/braise/coconut) but starch and spice profile genuinely differ, so kept as a distinct Kerala regional take that widens the catalog's South Indian coverage.

cross_protein_watch: Coconut-braise curries collide across proteins by structure. Decider should watch other selectors' pools for a Kerala/South-Indian coconut-tempering braise in pork, beef, or lamb (nadan varieties exist), and for any generic 'coconut curry' in turkey that shares the coconut-milk + onion + tomato + toasted-spice profile - those would be the same dinner in a different protein.
